data.description:
Spine task 1 of D1 v1. Produce docs/engineering/01-stack-decision.md: the framework/stack decision for the product app, in the form the front-end design plan (docs/design/00-frontend-design-plan.md) section 4 Phase C requires — options considered, criteria, a recommendation, and what would reverse it. Nothing else in the D1 build starts until this lands; every other v1 task depends on it transitively.

IMPLEMENTS: docs/engineering/00-d1-v1-milestone-plan.md section 3 row C-01 (IN by mandate — front-end design plan section 4 Phase C). Section 8.3 names it as spine task 1.

DECISION CONTEXT. The criteria are already fixed and are not re-derived here. The stack must be: (a) implementable by agent ICs working from text alone; (b) runnable under docker compose (infra rule, CLAUDE.md); (c) testable with NO external accounts — the right-sizing rule in milestone plan section 8.2 requires every task to name a verification method that works with the accounts we actually have, which is currently none; (d) free of paid services or licences; (e) able to keep every Stripe call behind a single enforceable chokepoint (the custody guard, the next spine task — see assumption A3, milestone plan section 5); (f) deployable to Digital Ocean when the deployment milestone opens (out of v1, but do not choose something that forecloses it); (g) able to consume the AS-29 design tokens (docs/design/tokens/tokens.css) without a build-step fight (front-end design plan section 5).

Our internal-tooling convention (zero dependencies, node --test, compose per app — see apps/chat/package.json) is EVIDENCE for this decision, not the decision. A product with a payment integration and real users may justify different answers; that is what this task is for. AS-31 named the slot and the criteria and deliberately named no candidates, because choosing a stack inside a scoping task is deciding in the wrong order.

VERIFICATION: the doc exists, names at least two real options, evaluates each against all seven criteria above, states a recommendation and the conditions that would reverse it. QA checks that every criterion is addressed for every option — this is a decision record, not a preference. Runnable now; no accounts, no code.

NOT IN THIS TASK: writing any application code (that is the scaffold task); choosing a hosting provider (Digital Ocean is already the infra rule); choosing a database engine beyond what the stack decision implies — if the stack leaves it open, say so and leave it to the data-model task.
data.title: D1 v1: stack decision for the product app (options, criteria, recommendation)

data.body:
SEQUENCING VERDICT: PROCEED. This task was flagged because two documents I authored on the same day disagree. docs/design/00-frontend-design-plan.md Phase C says the stack decision comes AFTER Phase B exists ('deciding a stack before the flows and the product are fixed is deciding in the wrong order'). The AS-31 plan and milestone plan section 8.3 make it spine task 1, ahead of AS-30. AS-30 has not run, so under Phase C's literal rule this task should not be starting. Resolved in the plan file section 2, not silently.

WHY PROCEED, shortest form: Phase C gave a rule ('after Phase B') and, in the same sentence, the REASON for the rule ('before the flows and the product are fixed'). The rule was a proxy for the condition. They coincided when written, because the product itself was still open. They have since come apart: the board fixed the product (step-5, 08-board-decision.md), and the milestone plan — which did not exist when Phase C was written — fixed the capability set (24 IN rows), the exact 7 screens and their routes, and a boundary filter that FORBIDS the surface growing, with 2 screens of headroom frozen. Phase B adds layout and states ledgers: depth on a fixed surface, not new surface.

Three supporting facts. (1) AS-36 and AS-30 are mutually independent and this is already on record in both directions — AS-30's own description says 'no framework/stack commitment is implied by this task', and its deliverable is framework-neutral static HTML. AS-30 is backlog with AS-29 done, i.e. pullable right now; proceeding delays it by zero. (2) Of the seven criteria, wireframes bear materially on at most one — (a) implementable-from-text, via the interactivity envelope — and that envelope is bounded by the capability table (no IN row for real-time state, offline, drag-drop, rich text, canvas or charts) rather than by wireframes. Criterion (g) is settled by a DELIVERED artifact: tokens.css states 'no build step, safe to link directly'. (3) Applied literally today, Phase C's rule INVERTS section 4.4 of its own document: AS-36 gates AS-37 which gates the whole server fan, so gating AS-36 on wireframes puts every non-UI task in v1 behind a design deliverable nothing else waits on — the exact failure the ready-queue invariant was built to prevent.

I am the author of both documents and therefore the party most tempted to rule the newer one right. Plan section 2.3 states the blocking steelman at full strength and answers it not with confidence but with a mechanism: the residual risk becomes reversal trigger T1 (observable, threshold, priced action), and separability of the front-end choice from the server choice is promoted to criterion (h) so a wrong front-end call costs the four UI tasks and never the server fan. Taking the objection seriously is what produced (h).

NOT CLAIMED: that Phase C was wrong when written. It was right — on 2026-08-31 morning the product was genuinely undecided and D1/C2/D4 are different technical shapes. Its error is narrower: it stated a proxy where it meant a condition, and the world moved.

AMENDMENT: docs/design/00-frontend-design-plan.md Phase C is the losing document and is amended in the implementation tick, wording given verbatim in plan section 3. docs/ is engineering-owned and I authored the file; NO top-level markdown needs changing (checked — README's only mention is a directory-map row that stays true), and employees never edit those anyway. The original sentence is preserved in quotation inside the amendment rather than deleted: records here are amended in the open. Acceptance criterion 10 checks the amendment landed, because without it the repo holds two contradictory sequencing rules and the next agent gets to pick which to obey.

WHAT THE PLAN SETTLES: criteria as GATES (compose, tests with no accounts AND no network egress, $0, enforceable Stripe chokepoint) vs ranked DISCRIMINATORS (implementable-from-text > separability > tokens-without-a-build-fight > DO-deployable, which has near-zero discriminating power and is recorded as such), combined LEXICOGRAPHICALLY rather than by weighted score — invented weights are unfalsifiable and hide which criterion actually decided, and a lexicographic rule makes the decisive criterion nameable, which is what a reversal clause needs. Ties go to the incumbent, declared in advance so a challenger must WIN a discriminator rather than merely match. Candidate rule: exactly 3, varying ONE AXIS AT A TIME (dependency policy; rendering model) so the outcome is attributable to an axis rather than a brand, with the fourth cell excluded-with-reason in the style of the capability table's OUT rows. No technologies are named in this plan, on purpose — same reason AS-31 named the slot and no candidates.

SPIKE: yes, warranted, and narrow. One screen — the invoice create/edit server half (repeating line-item group, server-side field-level validation, tokens.css, one stubbed Stripe call behind a module boundary) — built in each surviving candidate. Six measurements including gate (c) executed with egress blocked, and cold-error legibility (introduce one typo, record verbatim what the implementer sees). An IC who cannot see the error cannot debug and has nobody to ask. Gates first, eliminate, spike only survivors. Scratchpad only, fresh directory per candidate, nothing committed — a stray apps/ spike dir would be permanently un-cleanable under the shared-worktree rule. $0. One-tick box; on expiry, publish with gaps labeled and proceed.

CHAT APP: evidence, not precedent. It genuinely evidences that agent ICs can build and MAINTAIN a zero-dependency Node app under compose across 25+ merged tasks. It does not reach: no third-party integration (so the SDK-vs-hand-rolled question, which interacts with the custody chokepoint, is untested), no untrusted users (CSRF/sessions/cookie flags/escaping are what frameworks give free and hand-rolled code gets wrong — the strongest argument against extrapolating it), and public/app.js is 46,868 bytes in ONE hand-rolled file, 66%% of its front-end JS — a warning, not a template, and the doc must PROJECT that size for 7 screens x ~5 states rather than hand-wave it.

TIME-BOX: one tick for the whole task, spike included. AS-36 is spine task 1 with fourteen tasks behind it; a decision with a labeled gap beats no decision, because the reversal triggers make it recoverable. No branch, no worktree — documents and .lattice only, direct to master, no push (plan section 13). Reviewer should start with plan section 11.1: read criteria and evidence, STOP before the recommendation, write your own ranking, then compare.

DECISION LANDED: docs/engineering/01-stack-decision.md (980 lines, commit 58b1c3c). No branch/worktree per plan §13 — documents only.

RECOMMENDATION: build apps/invoicing in the C2 shape — server-rendered Node, small deliberate dependency budget. Node 24 · Express 5 (MIT) · EJS 6 (Apache-2.0), one template per screen · hand-rolled validation · node --test · docker compose with a network_mode:none test service · node:sqlite · hand-rolled Stripe client. Net adopted footprint: 2 direct packages.

RANKING C2 > C1 > C3. DECISIVE CRITERION: discriminator (a), implementable from text alone — specifically the IC context cost measurement (bytes an implementer must read to add one field): C2 18,076 · C1 28,029 · C3 36,812. Lexicographic ordering stopped at discriminator 1; (h)/(g)/(f) corroborate but did not decide.

GATES: all four adjudicated on executed evidence; NO eliminations. (b) compose config valid ×3. (c) suites re-run by me under --network none: exit 0, 5/5 each, 784ms/1941ms/1464ms — instrument validated first with both controls (EAI_AGAIN blocked, status 200 with network). (d) full transitive licence scan. (e) mutation-tested: ban removed -> suite red, restored -> green.

SPIKE (same invoice create/edit screen, 3 fresh scratchpad dirs, nothing committed):
· hand-written lines 937 / 927 / 1,563 — C1 and C2 within 1%, falsifying 'zero deps costs much more code'
· packages 0 / 67 / 30 · disk 0 / 12MB / 366MB · image delta +0 / +11 / +471 MB
· M5 cold-error legibility REVERSED on re-measurement: C1 and C2 suites CATCH the injected typo (4 pass/1 fail); C3's passes 5/5 green — its form is a client component node --test never renders. C3's tsc gives the best message but only if typecheck is in the loop.
· M6 tokens.css byte-identical (12,199) in C1/C2; C3 rewrites it to 7,224 and injects --lightningcss-* properties — criterion (g) failure.

Q1 CLOSED — hand-rolled Stripe client, not the SDK. Decided on (e) surface-to-ban. Executed probe: the SDK emitted the forbidden shape (transfer_data[destination], no Stripe-Account header) unchallenged, and a rogue 'new Stripe()' bypassed the wrapper entirely, so the SDK needs a parameter ban PLUS a source-level import ban. Hand-rolled builder 22 lines blocks both at the wire; webhook verification 11 lines with node:crypto, all three failure modes caught offline. NOTE: the SDK measured 1 direct / 0 transitive deps — that killed my own footprint argument against it, so Q1 rests on enforceability alone.

Q2 CLOSED — node:sqlite. Executed: Postgres reachable on a docker network but 'CANNOT reach: EAI_AGAIN' under --network none; sqlite runs with zero networking. Postgres does NOT fail gate (c) as worded (a bridge is not egress) — SQLite simply satisfies the strongest form, making the gate a one-word proof. AS-39 keeps SQL behind a data-access module; money as integer minor units + currency column (row C-32).

ZOD REJECTED from C2's assigned representative by the dependency policy's own rule 1: 150 lines/5,244B vs 124 lines/3,914B hand-rolled — it ADDED code.

PHASE C AMENDMENT LANDED verbatim in docs/design/00-frontend-design-plan.md, original sentence quoted not deleted.

DIVERGENCES / DEFECTS, all recorded in the doc's amendment log rows 5-7:
1. The plan's §3 amendment text cites '§4.4 of this very plan'; that document HAS no §4.4. Applied verbatim anyway because criterion 10 checks for exactly that wording and silently fixing a citation inside a verbatim block defeats the check. Correct target is milestone plan §8.1. FLAGGING AS A PLAN DEFECT.
2. Gate ordering: (d) pre-screened from registry metadata before any spike existed (eliminated nobody); (b)/(c)/(e) need a runnable artifact for executed evidence so were adjudicated post-build. Outcome identical.
3. Spike model substituted after all three launches failed on a rate limit before starting — same substitute for all three, comparison unaffected.
4. Self-check found and fixed: I claimed app.js was the largest file in the company; it is the largest APPLICATION source file (two docs files are bigger). Corrected.

SELF-CHECK: blind re-derivation run before hand-off — a fresh reviewer given the doc truncated before §10 independently returned C2 > C1 > C3 on criterion (a) via M4, matching the recommendation it had not read. It found 6 defects, all fixed: no threshold for 'genuinely tied' (now defined, with the after-the-fact weakness admitted), (h) adjudicated in adjectives (now measured: framework-touching files C2 1 / C1 2 / C3 7), (a)'s sub-measures had no combination rule (now lexicographic), friction tallies unlabelled, 4 unbacked superlatives, 2 arithmetic slips.

FOR QA (§11 protocol): do the blind re-derivation FIRST, before reading §10. Then the number audit — every comparative adjective must have a number. The two calls most worth challenging: (1) whether a 35% M4 gap really clears 'genuinely tied', since if it does not, the pre-declared tie-break hands this to C1; (2) whether supply-chain footprint (0 vs 67 packages) SHOULD have been a discriminator — under the criteria fixed in advance it is only a gate, and I deliberately did not let it back in after seeing results. That is a criteria-level amendment if the company disagrees.

Status transition and push left to the orchestrator.
